strokes.text: `terraform-provider-obs` manages an OBS Studio scene collection as Terraform resources: scenes, sources, groups, filters and the placements that arrange them.
It talks to OBS over obs-websocket 5 and, for the group operations that obs-websocket does not expose, through a small native plugin that ships in this repository.
Every write is read back from OBS before it is reported as done, and the provider refuses to write while OBS is streaming or recording.
how-it-connects | Terraform drives the obs provider, which reaches scenes and sources through obs-websocket and reaches groups through the native bridge plugin inside OBS Studio.
Documentation
The full reference is on the Terraform Registry, starting at @index.
@guides/getting-started builds a first scene with a source and a filter.
@guides/ownership-and-ordering explains anchors, extra placements and layer order.
@guides/groups covers the group resources and the native plugin they need.
@guides/filters-and-plugins covers generic and typed filters and plugin kinds.
@guides/importing brings existing scenes and sources under management.
@guides/verified-writes describes the checks around every write.
@guides/troubleshooting lists the refusals you are most likely to meet.
Use
Declare the provider and run `terraform init`:
ex:provider
Requirements
OBS Studio with obs-websocket 5 enabled; the provider is verified against OBS 32.2.2 with obs-websocket 5.7.4.
A base canvas of 1920x1080, or another size set in the provider block.
Terraform 1.5 or later.
The native bridge plugin from `native-bridge`, only for group resources, which today means macOS on Apple silicon.
How a Write Works
Before it writes, the provider checks that the right scene collection is active, that the canvas has the expected size and that nothing is streaming or recording.
After it writes, it reads the object back and reports success only when every field matches.
a-verified-write | A write passes a check, the write itself, a read back and a comparison, and ends as done, refused, or failed and tainted.
Who Owns What
A source resource owns the source and its first placement, called the anchor.
Each further placement is an `obs_scene_item`, and one `obs_scene_contents` per scene declares the layer order.
who-owns-what | One camera source is created with its first placement in the Office scene and reused by a second placement in the Gameplay scene.
Resources
Development
make build
make test
make vet
make docs
make docs-check
Tests run offline against scripted obs-websocket fakes.
The files under `docs` and the generated examples are rendered by `make docs` from the canvases in `tools/easel/canvas` and are never edited by hand.
Text is laid one sentence at a time with the easel, which checks every name it mentions against the provider schema and source.
Releases are cut by pushing a version tag, and the release workflow builds and signs the archives that the Registry expects.
